note: Steep wooded Missouri River bluffs and Nodaway River bottoms northwest of St. Joseph. MDC marks three primitive camping areas, each beside a small gravel lot: at the west end off the road from Route U (this one, in the trees beside a lot at a road bend), off County Road 325 at the north end (on open grass beside the lot), and off County Road 340 by the railroad. No amenities. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: three map/GIS-designated primitive camping areas, each beside a small lot (pin = GIS 258, under canopy 40 m SW of lot 903). Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights now manual. Pin move onto the lot suggested; phone matches; not waterfront kept; no split.
flags: INCLUSION OK: area page 'Things to Do: Camping: Individual Campsites | Boat-in along Missouri River'; brochure 'Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map.'; the map (© 09/15) has three 'Primitive Camping Area' symbols, each beside a Parking lot; GIS 27 points 257-259. Rule 140 standard; no special-use-only rule, no Rule 101.

PIN: stored 39.93109,-95.02087 = GIS 258, under continuous canopy 40 m SW of lot 903 (39.93140,-95.02062) with no visible track into the trees, so a rig would stay at the lot. Suggest 39.93140,-95.02062 (the lot: a gravel widening ~25 x 20 m where the area's gravel road bends, gate to a service track on its S side). A 23-ft rig reaches it on the gravel road from Route U; no ford or posted limit.

CLUSTERS (no split): GIS 257 (39.93671,-95.00814) on open grass ~40 m SE of lot 900, a ~30 x 20 m gravel pad at the end of a drive off County Road 325, 1.25 km NE - the most open of the three; GIS 259 (39.91052,-95.00313) under canopy N of lot 902 on County Road 340 beside the railroad, 2.7 km SE. Each is a single small lot, so none qualifies for a split. If a single best spot is wanted for the pin, the County Road 325 spot (open ground beside its lot) is the better camp; otherwise the lot suggestion above.
WATERFRONT: not waterfront kept. All three spots are 300 m+ from the Nodaway and Missouri rivers on the map.
HORSES: brochure 'Bicycles and horses allowed on multi-use trails' - no horse camp.
